stories.headline: Red Sox commit to Chad Tracy, Craig Breslow through 2030
stories.summary: The Red Sox signed Chad Tracy to a three-year contract as manager while also exercising the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.
stories.body:
The Boston Red Sox, who are heading to the postseason following a remarkable run over the second half of the season, rewarded the two chief architects of that turnaround Tuesday.

Boston removed the interim tag and named Chad Tracy the 49th manager in team history, signing him to a three-year contract that will run through the 2029 season, with a club option for 2030. The Red Sox also announced that they have exercised the 2029 and 2030 options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

The elevation of 41-year-old Tracy comes after the Red Sox secured a wild-card spot in the playoffs Sunday. Tracy took over in April after former manager Alex Cora was fired following a 10-17 start to the season.

Tracy has since guided the Red Sox to a 74-55 record, which included a 15-game win streak that tied the franchise record set in 1946. Boston's 27-3 (.900) record from July 3 through Aug. 7 was the best 30-game span in franchise history.

It's a remarkable turnaround for a team that was 32-46 and 15½ games back in the American League East race on June 24.

"Craig and Chad are two exceptionally talented leaders who have earned these opportunities in very different ways," Red Sox president Sam Kennedy said in a statement. "Over the last three years, we have watched Craig bring clarity, discipline, and conviction to the work of building our baseball operation. Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization.

"What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic. Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character, and the ability to bring out the best in others. Craig and Chad have demonstrated all of those qualities, and they have earned our confidence in leading us forward."

Breslow, 46, was hired in October 2023. A 2013 World Series champion with Boston, he is only the fourth former Red Sox player to lead the club's baseball operations efforts.

In his three seasons in the role, the Red Sox have gone 254-226 (.529), the third-best record in the AL.

Tracy had served as the manager of the Red Sox's Triple-A team in Worcester since 2022, leading the WooSox to a winning record in each of his four full seasons as manager. That came after seven previous years managing in the Los Angeles Angels' minor league system.

A third-round pick by the Texas Rangers in the third round of the 2006 draft out of Pepperdine University, Tracy also played eight professional seasons (2006-13) in the Rangers, Colorado Rockies and Kansas City Royals organizations.

stories.headline: Fantasy football rankings for Week 3: IDP
stories.summary: Weekly fantasy football draft rankings for IDP leagues from Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.
stories.body:
Each week during the 2026 NFL season, these fantasy football IDP rankings will be updated by fantasy analysts Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.

We've split up our fantasy football rankings by traditional IDP (individual defensive players) positions: defensive line, linebacker and defensive back. Scoring systems can vary greatly in IDP formats, so these rankings are based on the following scoring criteria:

Solo tackle: 1.5 points
Assisted tackle: 0.75 points
Tackle for loss: 2 points
Sack: 4 points
Interception: 5 points
Forced fumble: 4 points
Fumble recovery: 4 points
Defensive TD: 6 points
Safety: 2 points
Pass defensed: 1.5 points

stories.headline: Estêvão on reduced game time at Chelsea: 'I try to seize every opportunity I have'
stories.summary: Estêvão says he is focused only on what he can control after struggling for game time at Chelsea under new manager Xabi Alonso.
stories.body:
Estêvão says he is focused only on what he can control after struggling for game time at Chelsea under new manager Xabi Alonso.

The Brazilian winger has started only twice so far this season, on both occasions in the Carabao Cup.

He has been limited to just four late substitute appearances in the Premier League totalling 23 minutes and as such has not enjoyed the kind of impact that marked his debut campaign.

Alonso has favoured a front three of João Pedro, Cole Palmer and summer signing Morgan Rogers and all three have been key figures, scoring 10 goals between them, despite a mixed start to the manager's reign.

"I think every coach has their own way of playing," Estevao told a press conference while on international duty with Brazil. "Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day and that's what I do.

"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training, when I get an opportunity I try to give my best. It goes day after day."

The 19-year-old was a revelation last season and his introduction following his move from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025 was one of the only high points of a disappointing campaign for the club.

Highlights included a winning goal deep into stoppage time against Liverpool, who were the reigning Premier League champions at the time, and a brilliant individual strike in the 3-0 Champions League victory over Barcelona.

- Andre Villas-Boas hits back at John Terry's plane story: 'I see it different'

- Xabi Alonso joins unwanted managerial group after heavy Brentford defeat

- Lamine Camara better off in Monaco, ex-Chelsea midfielder says

He scored eight times in 36 appearances in all competitions en route to quickly winning over supporters at Stamford Bridge, who frequently sang his name.

Despite the team's poor defensive record so far under Alonso, they have mostly impressed going forward, scoring 18 times in seven matches, with Pedro, Palmer and Rogers especially catching the eye and thus limiting Estevao's opportunities.

"I try to seize every opportunity I have, I try to control everything I can and I leave it in God's hands and I trust myself a lot too," he said.

He was brought on three minutes from the end of Chelsea's defeat to west London rivals Brentford on Friday, with the team trailing 2-0. They conceded a further goal to eventually lose 3-0.

stories.headline: Stewart's 9-year no-tech streak snapped in Liberty's loss
stories.summary: Breanna Stewart's nine-year run of not getting a technical foul has come to an end after she picked one up in New York's 95-84 loss to Atlanta
stories.body:
Breanna Stewart's nine-year run of not getting a technical foul has come to an end after she picked one up in New York's 95-84 loss to Atlanta.

Stewart last got a technical foul in 2017 and now has three in her career after she was called for one in the waning minutes of the Liberty game on Monday night.

Stewart was upset that the officials didn't call a foul when she drove to the basket and Angel Reese stole the ball out of her hands with just under 2 minutes left in the game. Replays showed that Reese slapped Stewart's wrist.

"She slapped the s--- out of my hand," Stewart said talking about Reese. "You gotta see that."

Stewart had 27 points and 14 rebounds in the defeat, which ended the Liberty's chances of getting homecourt in the opening round of the playoffs that begin Sunday.

Stewart, who is second in the league in free throw attempts per game, said on the way out of the news conference that Reese should pay the fine that comes with the technical foul.

The two teams will play again on Wednesday in the regular-season finale.

The Liberty honored Stewart, along with the other six women's FIBA World Cup players on their roster. Stewart earned MVP of that tournament earlier this month, helping the U.S. win a fifth consecutive gold medal.

Information from ESPN's Alexa Philippou and The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: NBA Rank 2026, players Nos. 100-51: Four rookies make their debuts
stories.summary: We're revealing our top 100 players in the league for the 2026-27 season. Which players broke into Nos. 100 to 51? Which stars fell?
stories.body:
NBA Rank is back! With less than one month until opening night, let's start counting down the league's best players for 2026-27.

How many rookies landed in our top 100? Which stars who changed teams this summer are climbing our rankings? Where will the defending champion New York Knicks check in?

Our countdown begins with players Nos. 100-51 and continues Wednesday with Nos. 50-11 and Thursday with our expert panel's predictions for this season's top 10.

And that expert panel has been overhauled for the 2026 edition.

In previous seasons, more than 100 ESPN NBA insiders, reporters, editors and producers voted on thousands of possible player vs. player matchups to arrive at the final top-100 list.

That "wisdom of the crowd" approach has given way to the wisdom of seven: ESPN's Ben Golliver, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Bobby Marks, Dave McMenamin, André Snellings and Matt "Stats" Williams. (The panelists' individual top-100 lists were combined to create our final rankings.)

Voting guidelines, however, remained unchanged. The panel was asked to rank players based on predicted contributions -- quality and quantity -- for the 2026-27 regular season only.

Let's get to the list.

Note: Signature stats provided by ESPN Research.

100. Luguentz Dort
G | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 64

The Dorture Chamber heads southeast, where the Hawks will be downright scary on the wings with Dort, Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels. Dort is still one of the league's most physical defenders and is entering the final year of his contract (at $18.2 million), so he'll be motivated in a new environment. His 3-point shooting fell off last season after two years at a 40% clip with the Thunder. Even if last season was a regression to the mean, the physicality Dort brings is the sell for the Hawks. -- Vincent Goodwill

Signature stat: Dort defended 2026 All-Stars for 1,238 matchups last season, the third most in the NBA.

Fantasy projection: 9.6 PTS, 3.8 REB, 1.0 STL

99. RJ Barrett
G | Toronto Raptors

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 100

Barrett, the No. 3 pick in the 2019 draft, is a reliable secondary scorer who creates advantages with downhill attacks and plays well off lead options. Though the Toronto native hasn't developed into a franchise wing because of his mediocre outside shot and limited defensive impact, he thrilled his hometown fans in May with the signature moment of his seven-year career. When Barrett bounced home a last-second 3-pointer to beat the Cavaliers and force Game 7 in the Raptors' first-round playoff series, fans indulged in their most raucous celebration since the 2019 championship parade. -- Ben Golliver

Signature stat: Barrett shot 64% on layups and dunks last season, best in a season in his career and up from 55% in 2024-25, per GeniusIQ tracking.

Fantasy projection: 19.7 PTS, 5.6 REB, 3.9 AST

98. Jalen Suggs
G | Orlando Magic

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 59

Suggs excelled at forcing turnovers last season, ranking sixth in steals per game among players to appear in at least 50 games. He also averaged a career high in defensive net points per 100 possessions, per ESPN Analytics. Health will be a factor to watch for Suggs, who has missed at least 25 games in four of his five NBA seasons. There might be questions around Suggs and Anthony Black for the point guard role, but they did share the floor for 459 minutes last season. The Magic had a plus-13.5 net efficiency in that time. -- Matt Williams

Signature stat: The Magic shot 55.5% directly off Suggs' passes last season, second best in the NBA among players with at least 400 assist opportunities, according to GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 13.2 PTS, 4.0 AST, 1.5 STL

97. Caleb Wilson
F | Chicago Bulls

Age: 20

2025 NBA Rank: NR (rookie)

Wilson is the first of four rookies on this list, which befits the No. 4 pick from the most recent draft. He's an extraordinary athlete with immense potential, and he even flashed unexpected 3-point range at summer league (42% on 7.8 attempts per game). Like all rookies, he'll undergo growing pains this season -- he committed 21 turnovers to just seven assists during summer league -- but he's the Bulls' most compelling prospect since Derrick Rose. -- Zach Kram

Signature stat: Wilson was the second freshman to lead North Carolina in scoring, rebounding and steals in a season, joining Tyler Hansbrough in 2005-06.

Fantasy projection: 17.9 PTS, 8.1 REB, 1.4 BLK

96. Peyton Watson
F | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Watson's impact last year with Denver and his role this season has him cracking the top 100 for the first time. Before injuring his right hamstring Feb. 4, Watson was averaging 14.9 points while shooting 49.6% from the field and 41.7% on 3-pointers. (His 53% clip on corner 3s last season ranked sixth in the NBA among players with at least 1,000 minutes.) Following his offseason trade, Watson is likely to slide into the starting small forward role with Cleveland. -- Bobby Marks

Signature stat: Watson ranks second in field goal percentage allowed as the contesting defender since entering the league in 2022-23 among players to challenge at least 2,000 shots.

Fantasy projection: 14.2 PTS, 5.0 REB, 1.3 BLK

95. Donovan Clingan
C | Portland Trail Blazers

Age: 22

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Clingan makes his NBA Rank debut after developing into a reliable big in his second year in the league. He played 77 games and ranked third among all players in rebounds per game (11.6) and fifth in blocks (1.7). The 7-2 center will play for his third pro coach in as many seasons, with Micah Nori now roaming the sidelines in Portland. Clingan's crucial next step will be having his offense catch up to his defense. After averaging 12.1 points on 52% shooting in the regular season, he put up just 7.0 points on 30.4% shooting in a first-round loss to the Spurs. -- Dave McMenamin

Signature stat: Clingan led the NBA in offensive rebounds and contested shots on defense last season.

Fantasy projection: 11.4 PTS, 11.1 REB, 1.7 BLK

94. Coby White
G | Charlotte Hornets

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 71

White will get an upgraded role for the Hornets after they traded LaMelo Ball. White signed a large extension this offseason and moves into the starting guard spot after serving as a sixth man to end last season. White's career-best averages in points (20.4) and assists (5.1) came as a starter in Chicago. He has a solid chance to top those numbers as the Hornets' new quarterback. -- André Snellings

Signature stat: White ranked ninth in points per direct drive among 73 players to record at least 500 drives last season, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 20.0 PTS, 4.8 AST, 4.1 REB

93. Draymond Green
F | Golden State Warriors

Age: 36

2025 NBA Rank: 51

It's no surprise that Green has fallen to the back of the top 100 as he enters his late 30s. If anything, it's a testament to his long track record of success and continued defensive prowess that he -- a player who hasn't averaged double-digit points since 2017-18 -- is still on this list at all. Green is only a year removed from a first-team All-Defensive campaign, and he remains an excellent passer for his position. He has slipped just enough from his peak to no longer be realistically included in the All-Star conversation. -- Kram

Signature stat: Green averaged 4.6 3-point attempts last season, the most in his career.

Fantasy projection: 8.7 PTS, 6.1 REB, 5.7 AST

92. Jimmy Butler III
F | Golden State Warriors

Age: 37

2025 NBA Rank: 18

Butler's free fall in the rankings is easily explained by the right ACL injury he sustained in January. The wing could be sidelined until January or February 2027, according to ESPN's Anthony Slater, and faces real questions about whether he can regain his pre-injury form. The six-time All-Star, 37, will be an unrestricted free agent next summer and therefore should be motivated to make an impact once he returns. Sadly, his partnership with Stephen Curry already looks like a case of "what could have been." -- Golliver

Signature stat: The Warriors went 23-15 with Butler and 14-30 without him last season.

Fantasy projection: 19.4 PTS, 5.4 REB, 5.1 AST

91. Fred VanVleet
G | Houston Rockets

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

VanVleet is back with Houston after missing 2025-26 because of a torn ACL. Though last season's Rockets were in the top 10 in offensive efficiency, they ranked 27th in turnover percentage and 29th in that stat during clutch time. VanVleet will surely improve those figures; he was seventh in assist-to-turnover ratio in his last full season in 2024-25. -- Williams

Signature stat: VanVleet ranks seventh in career assist-to-turnover ratio among players to record at least 3,000 assists since individual turnovers were first tracked in 1977-78.

Fantasy projection: 14.0 PTS, 6.0 AST, 1.3 STL

90. Ayo Dosunmu
G | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: NR

After signing a five-year, $112 million contract in the offseason, Dosunmu is projected to have a significant role -- even with Minnesota's addition of LaMelo Ball. The Timberwolves are expected to be without guard Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) for an extended period. Acquired at the 2025 trade deadline from Chicago, Dosunmu averaged 14.4 points, and shot 52.1% from the field and 41.4% from 3 in his 24 games with Minnesota. -- Marks

Signature stat: In Game 4 against the Nuggets last postseason, Dosunmu had 43 points, the most in a playoff game off the bench since Fred Brown in 1976.

Fantasy projection: 15.3 PTS, 3.9 AST, 3.6 REB

89. Josh Hart
F | New York Knicks

Age: 31

2025 NBA Rank: 69

Hart enters 2026-27 after a title run and the best shooting season of his career. He shot 41% from 3-point range on nearly four attempts per game -- his most with the Knicks. And as New York's emotional barometer, Hart sounded the alarm after a March loss in Houston; the Knicks reeled off five straight wins before their season finale and title run. If the Knicks show slippage during their defense, Hart will call it out. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Hart shot 5.3% above expectation on 3-pointers last season, third best among players to attempt at least 200 threes, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 12.2 PTS, 7.7 REB, 5.0 AST

88. Matas Buzelis
F | Chicago Bulls

Age: 21

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The Bulls' high-flying forward virtually doubled his production from his rookie to sophomore seasons to crack NBA Rank for the first time. The 6-foot-8 Buzelis boosted his averages from 8.6 to 16.3 points, from 3.5 to 5.8 rebounds and from 1.0 to 2.1 assists per game. How he meshes with Chicago's No. 4 pick, Caleb Wilson, will be paramount for his continued development in the Windy City. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Buzelis increased his scoring average by 7.7 points from 2024-25 to 2025-26, second-largest increase in the NBA, trailing Nickeil Alexander-Walker.

Fantasy projection: 16.7 PTS, 6.0 REB, 1.6 BLK

87. CJ McCollum
G | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 35

2025 NBA Rank: NR

The Hawks acquired McCollum in the Trae Young deal, and the move ignited their second-half run, during which they posted the seventh-best record in the NBA after the deal. More scoring guard than point guard, McCollum fit perfectly next to do-everything point forward Jalen Johnson. McCollum is the best perimeter shot creator on the team, and his shooting range lets him space the floor and generate good looks for his teammates. He joins Most Improved Player Nickeil Alexander-Walker and former steals champion Dyson Daniels to give the Hawks one of the most dynamic backcourts in the league. -- Snellings

Signature stat: McCollum ranked fifth in points per direct handoff among 69 players to receive at least 200 handoffs last season, according to GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 19.1 PTS, 3.9 AST, 3.4 REB

86. Norman Powell
G | Chicago Bulls

Age: 33

2025 NBA Rank: 82

Powell followed a career campaign in 2024-25 (21.8 points per game) with an almost identical season in 2025-26 (21.7), which earned him his first All-Star nod at 32 years old. It's a brilliant late-career renaissance for the veteran guard, who is a career 40% 3-point shooter and even averaged a career-best 2.5 assists last season. He'll now be tasked with spacing the floor and scoring for a young Bulls team that traded away much of its offense last season. -- Kram

Signature stat: Powell ranked fourth in points per touch among players to record at least 1,000 touches last season, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 24.0 PTS, 3.8 REB, 2.6 AST

85. Cameron Boozer
F | Memphis Grizzlies

Age: 19

2025 NBA Rank: NR (rookie)

The 19-year-old Boozer enters his rookie season as perhaps the most NBA-ready prospect in his class because of his strong physique, excellent feel and winning history. During his freshman season at Duke, the 6-foot-8 forward averaged 22.5 points, 10.2 rebounds and 4.1 assists while leading the nation in win shares. After the Grizzlies traded Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr., Boozer should have the chance to emerge as the team's lead scoring option in the first year of a long-term rebuild. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Boozer was the first underclassman to average at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and four assists in a season since Larry Bird in 1976-77.

Fantasy projection: 18.5 PTS, 7.9 REB, 3.1 AST

84. Alex Caruso
G | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 32

2025 NBA Rank: 53

Caruso dropped in these rankings from last year, but there is a case he should be higher in this edition. He had another standout season defensively, ranking first among qualified guards in defensive Net Points per 100 possessions, according to ESPN Analytics. Although not known for his offense, Caruso showed that side of his game in the Western Conference finals against the Spurs, averaging 14.9 points and shooting 50% on 3-pointers during the seven-game series. -- Williams

Signature stat: Caruso shot 45% on 3-pointers in the 2026 playoffs, up from 29% in the regular season.

Fantasy projection: 8.4 PTS, 3.6 REB, 1.7 STL

83. Darryn Peterson
G | Utah Jazz

Age: 19

2025 NBA Rank: NR (rookie)

Peterson might have been the NBA draft's biggest enigma, but those questions feel long gone after a critic-quieting performance in Las Vegas. But in the NBA, he won't be browbeaten in a losing environment. The Jazz can bring him along slowly with Jaren Jackson Jr., Lauri Markkanen and Keyonte George, who recently received an extension, already in the fold. Peterson won't have the weight of carrying a Jazz franchise that hasn't been in the playoffs since 2022. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Peterson averaged 20.2 points last season, the most by a freshman in Kansas history.

Fantasy projection: 19.4 PTS, 3.8 REB, 2.8 AST

82. Jrue Holiday
G | Portland Trail Blazers

Age: 36

2025 NBA Rank: 91

Holiday moves up nine spots from last year's top 100 despite playing his fewest games (53) since 2014-15 and turning 36 years old in June. Holiday continues to impact winning. Including 2025-26, Portland's first postseason appearance since 2021, Holiday has been on a playoff team six straight seasons. He joins a crowded backcourt this season with Damian Lillard and Ja Morant. -- Marks

Signature stat: Holiday averaged career highs in 3-point makes and attempts last season.

Fantasy projection: 12.6 PTS, 4.7 AST, 4.5 REB

81. Naz Reid
F | Charlotte Hornets

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 90

Reid has a new home after spending the first seven years of his career in Minnesota. The 6-9 big was part of the Timberwolves' swap with the Charlotte Hornets for LaMelo Ball and will fit his quick-release 3s and rim-running abilities alongside Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel this season. The move will likely come with a role change for the 2023-24 Sixth Man of the Year, as Reid is penciled in as a starter with the revamped Hornets. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Reid was one of three players to score at least 1,000 points off the bench last season.

Fantasy projection: 15.9 PTS, 7.1 REB, 1.1 BLK

80. Josh Giddey
G | Chicago Bulls

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Giddey nearly averaged a triple-double last season and had career highs in points, rebounds and assists. A major area of improvement for the 6-7 guard is his long-distance shooting; since joining the Bulls ahead of the 2024-25 season, Giddey has increased his 3-point percentage while almost doubling his 3-point volume. Still only 23 but entering his sixth season, Giddey is on a career upswing and will form the centerpiece, along with rookie forward Caleb Wilson, for the young Bulls. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Giddey had 13 triple-doubles last season, second most in a season in Bulls history, trailing Michael Jordan's 15 in 1988-89.

Fantasy projection: 18.5 PTS, 9.6 AST, 9.2 REB

79. Ajay Mitchell
G | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 24

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Second-year players don't typically fare well on Most Improved Player ballots, because many voters think their improvement should be expected. But that didn't stop Mitchell from placing fifth in the award's voting last season, as the 2024 second-rounder blossomed into a crucial contributor to one of the NBA's top teams.

Mitchell now serves as a reliable secondary playmaker behind back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and Mitchell is a sufficient enough perimeter defender not to be torched on the other end. Oklahoma City went 10-1 in playoff games in which Mitchell played last season, but just 1-3 without him as the Thunder lost to the Spurs after injuries to Mitchell and Jalen Williams. -- Kram

Signature stat: Last season, Mitchell ranked in the top 10 in net points per 100 possessions among qualified guards, per ESPN Analytics.

Fantasy projection: 12.2 PTS, 3.3 AST, 3.0 REB

78. AJ Dybantsa
F | Washington Wizards

Age: 19

2025 NBA Rank: NR (rookie)

Dybantsa, the Wizards' first No. 1 pick since John Wall in 2010, led the nation in scoring, averaging 25.5 points as a BYU freshman. A dynamic forward who excels at drawing contact, Dybantsa joins a Washington roster that includes a mix of recent first-round picks plus established veteran stars, Anthony Davis and Trae Young. Where Dybantsa falls in the Wizards' pecking order will shape his Rookie of the Year candidacy and the franchise's hopes of snapping a five-year streak of finishing in the lottery. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Dybantsa is the first player to lead the nation in scoring and then get selected No. 1 in the NBA draft since Glenn Robinson in 1994.

Fantasy projection: 20.1 PTS, 4.9 REB, 2.8 AST

77. Ja Morant
G | Portland Trail Blazers

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 33

Morant has a new home with the Trail Blazers, and the main topic will be his availability. He has played just 79 games the past three seasons. His new team has an abundance of backcourt players as coach Micah Nori rotates among Morant, Lillard, Holiday and Scoot Henderson (and eventually Shaedon Sharpe when he returns from a torn meniscus in his right knee). Morant will look to get back to the production he had earlier in his career with Memphis, where he averaged the most points for a career in Grizzlies history. -- Williams

Signature stat: Since his rookie season in 2019-20, Morant is one of just nine players to average at least 20 points and seven assists.

Fantasy projection: 21.0 PTS, 7.2 AST, 3.8 REB

76. Dillon Brooks
F | Phoenix Suns

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Dillon the Villain is now Dillon the culture changer. Last season, he averaged a career-high 20.2 points as the Suns were one of the surprise teams in the West. Brooks deserves some credit for that turnaround, and the Suns gave him a three-year extension. Houston went from 22 to 41 wins in Brooks' first season there, and Phoenix had a nine-win improvement last season. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Brooks ranked in the top 10 in made 2-point jumpers last season, according to GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 18.6 PTS, 3.6 REB, 1.0 STL

75. Cason Wallace
G | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 22

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Wallace joins the top 100 for the first time, primarily because of his defensive impact. Named All-Defense for the first time in his career, Wallace led all players in steals this season. During the regular season, Wallace held opponents to 41.6% shooting as the closest defender, the fifth-best mark in the NBA, per GeniusIQ. And in the playoffs, Wallace held Austin Reaves, Devin Booker, Stephon Castle and Jalen Green to a combined 25% on 3-pointers. Wallace has played at least 68 games in each of his first three seasons, including 82 in his rookie year. He is eligible to sign a rookie extension before the Oct. 19 deadline. -- Marks

Signature stat: Wallace led the NBA in total steals and deflections last season.

Fantasy projection: 8.4 PTS, 3.1 REB, 1.9 STL

74. Isaiah Hartenstein
C | Oklahoma City Thunder

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 56

Injuries have held Hartenstein to just 94 games over the past two seasons, but he has established his value while on the court as OKC's rugged interior centerpiece. He has averaged a double-double, but perhaps more importantly, he has been disruptive on defense while crashing the boards heavily on offense. Hartenstein's size and energy pair with the length and skill of Chet Holmgren to create one of the best big man combinations in the league. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Hartenstein ranked fifth in total defensive net points last season, per ESPN Analytics.

Fantasy projection: 9.5 PTS, 9.6 PTS, 3.5 AST

73. Walker Kessler
C | Los Angeles Lakers

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 98

Kessler's potential fit alongside Luka Doncic has him vaulting 25 spots on the NBA Rank list, despite playing just five games last season. The surgically repaired torn labrum in Kessler's left shoulder didn't discourage the Lakers from trading unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, plus pick swaps in 2028 and 2030 to pry the 7-2 center from the Jazz. L.A. inked Kessler to a four-year, $130 deal, banking on him to anchor the defense while providing Doncic an ideal lob partner. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Kessler has averaged 2.4 blocks in his career, second most since entering the NBA in 2022-23, trailing Victor Wembanyama.

Fantasy projection: 11.5 PTS, 12.4 REB, 2.6 BLK

72. VJ Edgecombe
G | Philadelphia 76ers

Age: 21

2025 NBA Rank: NR

It might seem natural that the No. 3 pick in the 2025 draft would finish third in Rookie of the Year voting, but that placement undersells Edgecombe's impressive debut season. As a Day 1 starter for a team that reached the second round of the playoffs, Edgecombe averaged 16.0 points, 5.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists while making 35% of his 3s. Perhaps most impressively, he ranked 11th in the league in minutes despite having to adjust to a full NBA schedule. -- Kram

Signature stat: Edgecombe played 2,623 minutes last season, the most by a rookie since Ben Simmons and Donovan Mitchell in 2017-18.

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 5.4 REB, 1.4 STL

71. Tyler Herro
G | Milwaukee Bucks

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 68

Herro endured a major one-two punch this summer: A few weeks after he was traded from the Heat to the Bucks, the scoring guard was on the wrong end of a physical altercation with former teammate Bam Adebayo in Las Vegas. A return to his hometown of Milwaukee offers a fresh start for the 2025 All-Star, who blossomed from sixth man to lead initiator during his seven-year run in Miami. Herro should enjoy a green light on the rebuilding Bucks, who must reconstruct their offense after parting with franchise legend Giannis Antetokounmpo. -- Golliver

Signature stat: According to GeniusIQ, Herro ranked second in points per direct isolation last season among players with at least 100 isolations, trailing Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

Fantasy projection: 22.5 PTS, 5.1 REB, 4.7 AST

70. Payton Pritchard
G | Boston Celtics

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 97

Pritchard saw a jump in usage as he became a consistent starter before shifting back to the bench in early February. Pritchard averaged career highs in points (17.0), rebounds (3.9) and assists (5.2). His touches per game also went from 51.8 in 2024-25 to 68.9 in 2025-26, the second-largest increase among 33 players to record at least 4,000 touches in each season, behind Portland's Deni Avdija. -- Williams

Signature stat: Pritchard started 50 games last season after making 17 starts across his first five seasons.

Fantasy projection: 16.0 PTS, 4.8 AST, 3.8 REB

69. Damian Lillard
G | Portland Trail Blazers

Age: 36

2025 NBA Rank: NR (injury)

It's hard to project Lillard's place in these rankings after he missed all of last season recovering from an Achilles injury, and especially with Morant joining the already-crowded backcourt. The last time Lillard played, he was still a 25-point scorer who shot 38% from 3-point range. Returning to Portland will be heartwarming as Lillard seeks a bounce-back season. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: After missing last season, Lillard will play for Portland for the first time since 2022-23. He has the most career points and second-most career assists in Trail Blazers history.

Fantasy projection: 21.7 PTS, 6.2 AST, 4.0 REB

68. Keyonte George
G | Utah Jazz

Age: 22

2025 NBA Rank: NR

Another newcomer to the list, George would have been a candidate for Most Improved Player if not for the league's 65-game rule. George was one of 18 players this season to increase their scoring average by at least 6.8 points and is one of 11 players to average at least 23 points and six assists last season. The arrivals of Jaren Jackson Jr. and Darryn Peterson should have Utah contending for a playoff spot this season. If that happens, expect George's ranking to improve in future seasons. The guard is eligible for a rookie extension until the Oct. 19 deadline. -- Marks

Signature stat: George is the second Jazz player with 3,000 points and 1,000 assists within his first three NBA seasons, along with Deron Williams.

Fantasy projection: 22.3 PTS, 6.1 AST, 3.7 REB

67. Paul George
F | Boston Celtics

Age: 36

2025 NBA Rank: 54

The Celtics will be George's fourth team after spending the first seven years of his career in Indiana. After a solid first-round performance for the 76ers in their seven-game series victory over Boston -- 17.4 points on 55% from 3 with 4.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.4 steals -- the Celtics traded for George as part of the stunning Jaylen Brown deal. Just like in all of his other spots, George will be contributing to a team expected to make noise in the postseason, and he'll be looking to make his third trip to a conference finals in his 17th season. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: George needs just two 3-pointers to pass Kyle Korver for eighth on the all-time list.

Fantasy projection: 19.8 PTS, 5.4 REB, 1.7 STL

66. Ivica Zubac
C | Indiana Pacers

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 36

Zubac entered last season fresh off a breakout campaign, during which he finished fourth in the league in rebounding (12.6 per game) while making second-team All-Defense. He was well on his way to averaging his second straight double-double before injuries interfered, and he was ultimately traded from the Clippers to the Pacers. This season, he is the interior anchor for a Pacers squad that will try to return to prominence with their core players healthy. Zubac's rebounding and defense will be a key to the Pacers' postseason aspirations. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Zubac held opponents to 49% shooting at the rim last season, fourth best among players to defend at least 200 shots, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 14.3 PTS, 10.9 REB, 1.1 BLK

65. Brandon Ingram
F | LA Clippers

Age: 29

2025 NBA Rank: 77

In the 2019-20 season, his first in New Orleans, Brandon Ingram won the Most Improved Player award. And he has produced at basically that level in all seven seasons since, averaging between 20 and 25 points every season and combining a high usage rate with roughly league-average efficiency.

But now, Ingram is on his third team in three seasons, as his overall impact doesn't match his shiny scoring totals. He'll continue to get buckets for the Clippers this season, but it's unclear how much he'll do beyond that. -- Kram

Signature stat: Ingram made 197 shots from the midrange last season, third most in the NBA, trailing DeMar DeRozan and Kevin Durant.

Fantasy projection: 22.6 PTS, 5.7 REB, 4.8 AST

64. Aaron Gordon
F | Denver Nuggets

Age: 31

2025 NBA Rank: 40

Gordon's impact on winning remains crystal clear: The Nuggets played at a 62-win pace with him in the lineup and a 48-win pace without him last season, then they crumbled in the first round of the playoffs as he battled a calf ailment. The veteran forward has averaged just 53 games played in the three years since Denver's 2023 championship run, and his rankings drop reflects growing concerns that he has become a chronic injury risk. Even so, Gordon's activity, experience and defensive versatility make him the perfect fit alongside Denver's star duo of Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Gordon has shot 41% on 3-pointers over the past two seasons after shooting 32% from beyond the arc across his first 10 seasons.

Fantasy projection: 15.5 PTS, 5.5 REB, 3.1 AST

63. Jarrett Allen
C | Cleveland Cavaliers

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 45

The Cavaliers will get a full season of Allen running on-ball screens with James Harden, an action they went to quite a bit after Harden arrived in Cleveland. According to GeniusIQ, Allen set 13.7 on-ball screens per game with Harden as the ball handler, ranking in the top five among duos to run 100 pick actions together from Feb. 7 until the end of the regular season. Allen also had a jump in his offensive production in the 13 regular-season games he played with Harden, averaging 18.4 points and 70.5% shooting from the field. -- Williams

Signature stat: Allen shot 64% from the field last season, fifth best in the NBA among qualified players.

Fantasy projection: 15.8 PTS, 10.0 REB, 1.0 BLK

62. Darius Garland
G | LA Clippers

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 38

The two-time All-Star slid down the NBA Rank list after playing just 45 games last season and being dealt from the Cavaliers to the Clippers. One encouraging sign for Garland's upcoming campaign is that the Clippers went 13-6 in the 19 games he played after the trade. As one of the 71 active players with 1,000 or more made 3-pointers in their career, Garland will be relied on to space the floor in coach Ty Lue's matchup-based offense. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Garland ranked 10th in points per direct pick last season among 51 players to run at least 1,000 on-ball screens as the ball handler, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 21.6 PTS, 7.4 AST, 1.3 STL

61. Mikal Bridges
F | New York Knicks

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 48

The NBA's current iron man sits eighth on the all-time list of consecutive games played (638) and could pass Harry Gallatin, Bill Laimbeer and Dolph Schayes this season. And Bridges settled into his role right as the playoffs rolled around last spring; his scoring was its lowest since 2022, but he shot a blistering 56% in the postseason and made several big shots in the Knicks' run. Perhaps it's something that extends to this season. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Bridge's iron man streak is the second-longest consecutive games streak to begin a career in NBA history, trailing Johnny Kerr (844).

Fantasy projection: 15.2 PTS, 3.7 AST, 1.2 STL

60. Michael Porter Jr.
F | Brooklyn Nets

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 70

A change in scenery helped Porter rise 10 spots in the rankings. Acquired last offseason from Denver, along with a 2032 unprotected first-rounder, Porter averaged a career-high 24.2 points and shot 36.3% on 3s, his fourth consecutive season shooting better than 36% from deep. Before suffering a strained left hamstring late in the season, Porter had missed just 14 games since 2023-24. He is on an expiring $40.8 million contract and is eligible for four additional years and up to $234 million. -- Marks

Signature stat: Porter had 14 games of scoring at least 30 points last season, more than double what he had in any other season of his career.

Fantasy projection: 23.5 PTS, 7.2 REB, 2.9 AST

59. Ausar Thompson
G | Detroit Pistons

Age: 23

2025 NBA Rank: NR

For all the fair questions about Thompson's shooting, his ability to be a defensive menace is undeniable. That was on display in last season's playoffs, when he recorded nearly four steals plus blocks per game. The Pistons just rewarded him with a deal that could be a steal in a couple of years even with modest improvement. If not for Victor Wembanyama, a Defensive Player of the Year award could be within reach. -- Goodwill

Signature stat: Thompson led the NBA in steals per game and ranked second in total deflections last season.

Fantasy projection: 10.4 PTS, 6.0 REB, 2.0 STL

58. Domantas Sabonis
F | Sacramento Kings

Age: 30

2025 NBA Rank: 34

Sabonis will look to bounce back after Sacramento's nightmare 2025-26 campaign, during which he played a career-low 19 games because of a season-ending knee surgery. Despite the first extended absence of his 10-year career, Sabonis remains a productive offensive lynchpin who ranks second leaguewide in double-doubles over the past five seasons. The 6-10 center stands out with energy and deft passing, but his lack of 3-point range and poor rim protection have made it challenging to construct a consistent winner around him. -- Golliver

Signature stat: Sabonis' three-year streak of leading the league in rebounds per game ended last season.

Fantasy projection: 18.9 PTS, 13.6 RPG, 6.8 AST

57. Trey Murphy III
F | New Orleans Pelicans

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 58

Murphy is one of the best examples of a 3-and-D player in the NBA, and he's one of the season's most appealing potential trade candidates for that reason. The 26-year-old is a career 38% 3-point shooter on high volume -- he ranked sixth among qualified players in 3-point makes per game last season -- and he has also increased his assist average in every season of his career, hinting at yet-untapped potential in his all-around offensive game. -- Kram

Signature stat: Last season, Murphy became the second player in league history with at least 200 3-pointers and 100 dunks in a season. Lauri Markkanen accomplished it in 2022-23.

Fantasy projection: 19.5 PTS, 5.2 REB, 3.4 AST

56. Jaden McDaniels
F | Minnesota Timberwolves

Age: 25

2025 NBA Rank: 75

Though McDaniels is often discussed for his defense, his offensive improvement is why he climbed 19 spots in the rankings. McDaniels had a career year, averaging his best marks in points (14.8), assists (2.7) and 3-point field goal percentage (41%). That was on display when McDaniels had a playoff career-high 32 points in Game 6 to eliminate the Nuggets in the first round. With Julius Randle and Naz Reid being traded this summer and Donte DiVincenzo missing at least most of the season because of a torn right Achilles, McDaniels will get a larger offensive workload even with Minnesota's acquisition of LaMelo Ball. -- Williams

Signature stat: McDaniels defended 2026 All-Stars for 1,163 matchups last season, fourth most in the NBA, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 14.2 PTS, 4.4 REB, 1.1 STL

55. Nickeil Alexander-Walker
G | Atlanta Hawks

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 96

In his first season with the Hawks, Alexander-Walker set career highs in scoring (20.8 points per game) and in efficiency, establishing himself as the starting shooting guard for one of the hottest teams in the NBA down the stretch of 2025-26. Alexander-Walker is a shooter/scorer who can create off the dribble or operate as a spot-up shooter, and is a disruptive defender. The reigning Most Improved Player has All-Star upside this season. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Alexander-Walker increased his scoring average by 11.4 points from 2024-25 to 2025-26, the largest increase in the NBA.

Fantasy projection: 19.2 PTS, 3.5 AST, 1.2 STL

54. Julius Randle
F | Brooklyn Nets

Age: 31

2025 NBA Rank: 42

Randle fell 12 spots despite averaging more than 20 points for a fifth time in six seasons. However, his regular-season production took a nosedive in the postseason. Randle averaged five fewer points while shooting 39% from the field and 24.4% on 3-pointers. Traded in the offseason from Minnesota to Brooklyn, expect Randle to improve the flow of the Nets' 30th-ranked offense. In the lineups where Minnesota did not play with a point guard, Randle averaged 5.0 assists per game. He has two years left on his contract, including a player option for 2027-28. -- Marks

Signature stat: Randle was one of four players to record at least 1,500 points, 500 rebounds and 300 assists last season.

Fantasy projection: 22.0 PTS, 8.1 REB, 5.0 AST

53. Jaren Jackson Jr.
F | Utah Jazz

Age: 27

2025 NBA Rank: 31

With the flurry of offseason activity, the Jazz's acquisition of the former Defensive Player of the Year in February is easy to overlook -- especially because Jackson suited up for the Jazz just three times after the trade. But his career averages of 18.6 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.9 blocks will make him a key cog alongside Lauri Markkanen, Keyonte George, Ace Bailey and No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson as Utah eyes its first postseason berth since 2022. -- McMenamin

Signature stat: Jackson ranked in the top 10 in effective field goal percentage allowed as the contesting defender among players to contest at least 800 shots, per GeniusIQ.

Fantasy projection: 21.9 PTS, 5.7 REB, 1.6 BLK

52. Desmond Bane
G | Orlando Magic

Age: 28

2025 NBA Rank: 39

Bane brought consistent 3-point shooting to the Magic, who desperately needed it. He also played in all 82 games on a team with a starting lineup that was otherwise ravaged by injury. He has averaged more than 20 points in three of the past four seasons, but it is his five straight seasons averaging at least two 3s per game on strong percentages that make him invaluable to the Magic's playoff aspirations. -- Snellings

Signature stat: Bane was one of four players to start all 82 games last season, along with Toumani Camara, Mikal Bridges and Donte DiVincenzo.

Fantasy projection: 20.7 PTS, 4.8 REB, 4.8 AST

51. Zion Williamson
F | New Orleans Pelicans

Age: 26

2025 NBA Rank: 61

The good news is that Williamson was mostly healthy last season, with his 62 games representing the second-highest total of his career. The bad news is that his impact was more muted than usual during that time. Williamson's usage rate and scoring average (21.0 points per game) were career lows.

During his first few seasons, Williamson was a high-risk, high-reward enigma. He was rarely healthy, but he produced at an All-Star level and looked frequently unstoppable when he was available. Yet now, he has seemingly settled into a more mundane existence in his mid-20s: Given his defensive limitations and lack of shooting range, Williamson is a tricky fit in a modern NBA lineup, and he hasn't made an All-Star team since 2023. -- Kram

Signature stat: Williamson averaged 15.4 paint points last season, the most in the NBA among players to appear in at least 40 games.

Fantasy projection: 22.8 PTS, 6.1 REB, 4.3 AST

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey draft strategy: The 2026 rookies who can make an impact this season
stories.summary: Looking for promising NHL rookies who can make an impact for your fantasy hockey team? Start here.
stories.body:
There's little debate about whether the following Calder candidates will make a considerable imprint in the NHL, the only real question is when. While both Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby erupted for more than 100 points as rookies, Nikita Kucherov collected only 18 in 52 games during his first NHL season. Nathan MacKinnon didn't start wowing us in the scoring department until Year 5. As with identifying any other breakout candidate, pegging which first-year players are ready to erupt immediately, then securing them ahead of or during the season, will make your fantasy team better.

To be clear, each of these young competitors should be accounted for in dynasty and keeper competition. This discussion is about whether they can help your redraft team right now, in 2026-27.

More: Sign up for free | Rankings | Projections | League types

Gavin McKenna, F, Toronto Maple Leafs

In my view, of this year's gaggle of talented rookies, June's No. 1 NHL draft pick sports the highest fantasy ceiling. While you can only gather so much intel from preseason play, McKenna already appears comfortable and dangerous. Whether he remains on a dynamite scoring unit with John Tavares and William Nylander, or earns a twirl alongside Auston Matthews, the Yukon native is going to score. Maybe more than any other rookie in 2026-27.

Compared to Kucherov as an elite playmaker-in-the-making with outstanding vision and a top-tier hockey IQ, McKenna should be accounted for in all fantasy leagues of reasonable size. Goodness gracious, this kid banged out 129 points in 56 games in his final round in Medicine Hat before amassing 51 in 35 contests at Penn State last year. Plus, he doesn't seem overwhelmed at all by playing in Toronto's hockey hotbed.

Porter Martone, F, Philadelphia Flyers

Neck and neck with McKenna as this year's top fantasy rookie -- many pundits will reasonably argue the Flyers winger should rank first overall -- Martone seems eager to take the next step after making an excellent first impression. We were all super impressed with the teen's four goals and six assists on 32 shots through only nine regular-season games this past spring (another five points in 10 playoff contests). Projected to skate in Philly's top-six and on the No. 1 power play, while providing a much-appreciated front-of-net presence, the young power forward is going to put up points and add some of the physical stats. If it wasn't for McKenna's outstanding talent and projected position in Toronto's lineup, Martone would serve as my top fantasy rookie to launch 2026-27.

Roman Kantserov, F, Chicago Blackhawks

He's going to score goals. Probably not at the rate of 0.57/game that led the KHL last year, but at a decent clip. If he maintains a spot on Chicago's top line and power play with Patrick Kane and (eventually) Connor Bedard, the 22-year-old might also find himself in the Calder conversation with others on this list. While I get the trepidation about linking fantasy arms with KHL exports -- it sometimes doesn't work out -- there are also enough success stories to appreciate. Remember when Artemi Panarin joined these same Blackhawks in 2015-16 and collected 77 points including 30 goals? Again, if afforded ample opportunities, Kantserov is going to shoot and score with regularity. Draft him late as a wild card in deeper leagues.

James Hagens, F, Boston Bruins

Don't expect the flashiest numbers from the 19-year-old if he sticks on a third line with Fraser Minten and Marat Khusnutdinov. But if Hagens ultimately climbs into the Bruins top six -- perhaps replacing Casey Mittelstadt -- and earns turns on the secondary power play, he could make more productive noise. After competing in five games between the regular season and playoffs this past spring, the seventh-overall draft selection (2025) is expected to remain in the NHL from start to finish. Draft the speedy and creative future center as a last-round flier in deeper leagues. Otherwise maintain him on your fantasy radar as action gets underway.

Anton Frondell, F, Chicago Blackhawks

I don't want to make too much about Frondell filling in for Bedard on the top line and power play since the Blackhawks captain isn't expected to miss that much time with his shoulder injury. Early November will be here before we know it. Instead, let's evaluate the 19-year-old through the fantasy lens as Chicago's regular second-line center, if Frank Nazar doesn't secure that gig, and participant on the secondary power-play. That brings us to a forecast season-long haul in the 55-60 point range. Hardly jaw-dropping, but solid for a teen center in his first year.

Make no mistake, as a burgeoning great player in this league, Frondell is going to build on his totals, year over year. I only think we should keep demands reasonable in his first full go around, even after the third-overall pick (2025) potted nine points in 12 contests last year. If you want to roll the dice on a robust October from the young Swede, go for it. Just have a plan in place for if/when he drops off once Bedard returns a month later.

ESPN Fantasy Hockey is the fun, free way to get inside the game. Draft your players, set your lineups and earn points when the pros do. Sign up today!

Ivar Stenberg, F, San Jose

Tapped the most NHL-ready skater of this year's draft crop after a successful run with Frolunda HC, Stenberg is expected to make an immediate impact in the NHL. ESPN draft analyst Rachel Kryshak suggests there's no question this year's second-overall selection makes the Sharks tangibly better, straight away:

"Stenberg is a tremendous talent, who is capable of impacting the game both offensively and defensively. Should he play his way onto Macklin Celebrini or Michael Misa's wing, there is a real opportunity for him to produce offensively. Regardless of where he plays, Stenberg is likely to have the best two-way impact of the entire rookie crop. Stenberg's combination of two-way play and offensive play-driving ability should be a major boost for the Sharks and may help put them over the top as a wild-card team this season."

While Sharks fans are concerned only about Stenberg helping his club fight for a playoff spot, we should probably temper our fantasy expectations. Lauded as a skilled two-way player, and prematurely poised to skate on a second line and secondary power play, Stenberg projects to earn 45 to 50 points in his first NHL season. Meaning, right now, his value appears limited in standard redraft competition. We'll see if that eventually changes via a possible line assignment with Celebrini.

Viggo Bjorck, F, Winnipeg Jets

Boy oh boy, if the 19-year-old manages to seize the second-line center position and nail down a spot on the secondary power play in Winnipeg, we may have a deep-league fantasy surprise on our hands. This year's eighth-overall draft pick could also start the campaign in the AHL. So, we're in wait-and-see mode for now.

Made it this far? Create your own league with your own rules and play against your friends today.

Cole Hutson, D, Washington Capitals

If we're to see a defenseman win the Calder Trophy for a third season in a row (which would be an NHL first), my money's on this kid. After collecting three goals and seven assists in 14 NHL games this past season, the youngest Hutson brother boasts the potential to serve as a top-25 fantasy defender in his first full campaign. Second behind fantasy heavyweight Jakob Chychrun on the Capitals, the Boston University alumnus is going to put up a minimum of 45 points this round. Draft the 20-year-old in deeper leagues after your top-two blue-line spots are filled.

Sebastian Cossa, G, Utah Mammoth

The former Detroit prospect is finally earning a legitimate shot at proving himself in the NHL. After three quality seasons with the Grand Rapids Griffins, the 15th-overall draft pick (2021) is going to earn turns behind Mammoth No. 1 Karel Vejmelka. If all goes to plan in Utah, we can probably expect 25 games or so out of Cossa as Vejmelka is again expected to earn the bulk of starts. But you never know. If the veteran falls hurt or struggles otherwise, the 23-year-old could be busier for a pretty good team in Salt Lake City. While the rookie netminder isn't currently worth drafting out of the gates, he could emerge as a midseason fantasy replacement or streaming option as 2026-27 unfolds.

Jacob Fowler, G, Montreal Canadiens

The Canadiens claim they're committed to running with two, not three, netminders this season. Right now that seems to be Jakub Dobes and Fowler, leaving Sam Montembeault out in the cold. If so, what does this timeshare look like? After Dobes made such a positive impression in his first regular season, and through three rounds of the playoffs, Fowler could see limited playing time. On the other hand, if Dobes doesn't equal last year's impressive showing, the 21-year-old goalie could earn more chances with a very competitive Canadiens squad. Through the fantasy lens, this is another goaltending situation to monitor closely when the games start to matter.

See also:

Sergei Murashov, G, Pittsburgh Penguins
Ilya Protas, F, Washington Capitals
Victor Eklund, F, New York Islanders

stories.headline: Arman Tsarukyan elevates his position in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

stories.headline: Dillon: Dockers might still have Wharfie Time at GF
stories.summary: Despite reports Fremantle's unique motivator for players and fans would not be permitted when they meet Brisbane at the neutral venue MCG on Saturday, AFL chief Andrew Dillon says a decision has not yet been made.
stories.body:
The bell might not have tolled for 'Wharfie Time' at the AFL grand final after all.

Despite reports Fremantle's unique motivator for players and fans would not be permitted when they meet Brisbane at the neutral venue MCG on Saturday, AFL chief Andrew Dillon says a decision has not yet been made.

Appearing on AFL 360 on Tuesday night, Dillon indicated the Dockers' push to have Wharfie Time enacted, if needed, had some merit.

"We've had the clubs in today going through the operational aspects of the game," he said.

"As we've seen during the finals this year, the home side has got the ability to make it like a home final.

"We're just working through the finer details of that with both of the clubs at the moment, because at a grand final we don't have a home team per se, it's a neutral game.

"So how those goal celebrations play out, how a potential for Wharfie Time might be, we've got to dot some Is and cross some Ts there.

"I think there's been some reporting that it has been banned. There hasn't been a decision for or against at the moment. We're working through it."

Dillon experienced Wharfie Time at Fremantle's home semi-final win against Geelong and described it as "amazing".

Asked if he was considering its use at the grand final more favourably than he had been in recent days, Dillon said: "It came to my attention, I didn't think it was as big a deal as what it is.

"But absolutely, it's important for our fans and so that's why we're looking at it through that lens.

"But we've got to make sure it's respectful of the football and everything else as well."

Dillon was reminded Brisbane had goal celebration songs played during their 2025 grand final win over Geelong, such as Charlie Cameron's famous anthem, John Denver's 'Take Me Home, Country Roads'. Songs will again be permitted after goals this Saturday.

"That's what we're working through. If we have that for the Brisbane Lions, which has worked well, then what's the Fremantle equivalent and how that plays out?" Dillon said.

Wharfie Time, highlighted by the ominous tolling of bells, has previously only been used at Perth's Optus Stadium and has been a rare occurrence, with Fremantle keen to maintain a sense of mystique around the motivator.

The button was famously pushed to inspire a come-from-behind win over Hawthorn in May and again in a close finish to the Dockers' semi-final win over Geelong.

stories.headline: Ugo Ugochukwu celebrates Nigerian roots after winning FIA Formula 3 championship
stories.summary: Newly crowned FIA Formula 3 champion Ugo Ugochukwu says he is proud to represent his Nigerian heritage on the international stage, even though he races under the United States flag.
stories.body:
Newly crowned FIA Formula 3 champion Ugo Ugochukwu says he is proud to represent his Nigerian heritage on the international stage, even though he races under the United States flag.

Ugochukwu, whose mother is Nigerian supermodel Oluchi Onweagba-Orlandi, became the first American to win the FIA Formula 3 championship after finishing second in the season-ending Feature Race in Madrid earlier this month.

He said during a post-race interview on SuperSport that his Nigerian heritage is a matter of pride: "I think it's amazing. I'm super proud of my Nigerian roots, on my mom's side.

"For me, it makes me very proud every time I can get on the podium, get my name out there to everyone watching and supporting in Africa. That means a lot and hopefully I can be a good role model to all the kids who would like to have this dream as well."

The 19-year-old entered the final weekend 15 points behind Britain's Freddie Slater, but drew level before last Sunday's race after qualifying and Saturday's Sprint Race.

Starting second behind Finland's Tuukka Taponen, Ugochukwu held his position to the finish while Slater came home eighth. The result gave the Campos Racing driver the championship with 159 points, 14 clear of Slater.

"There was a little bit of pressure, which is pretty normal," he said while describing the championship decider. "This last weekend was definitely the most important one of the championship."

With the hard part done in qualifying, the Ugochukwu said his priority in the final race was to protect the position he needed to secure the title, instead of chasing Taponen for the victory and putting it all at risk.

"We knew that was what I needed to win the championship, so it was just about getting it home," he said.

The championship win has attracted even more attention in Nigeria, where his maternal heritage means that Nigerians have followed his progress through the international racing ranks, all the way from his go-carting beginnings.

Born in New York to Onweagba-Orlandi and Italian fashion designer Luca Orlandi, Ugochukwu represents the United States in international competition. His mother won the inaugural M-Net Face of Africa competition in 1998 before going on to an international modelling career that included work with some of the world's leading fashion houses.

This Nigerian connection has previously brought public recognition from prominent Nigerians. After he won the Macau Grand Prix in 2024, Nigerians in Diaspora Commission Chair Abike Dabiri-Erewa congratulated him, while former presidential candidate Peter Obi also celebrated the achievement, pointing to his Nigerian heritage.

That Macau victory made Ugochukwu the first American to win the event since Bob Earl in 1981 and added to a record that already included the 2020 FIA Karting European Championship junior title and the inaugural Euro 4 Championship in 2023.

He added the Formula Regional Oceania championship earlier this year before returning for his second season in Formula 3.

His first F3 campaign with PREMA Racing in 2025 produced two podium finishes and 16th place in the championship. Now, the move to Campos Racing for 2026 has brought an immediate improvement, beginning with victory in the opening Feature Race in Melbourne.

Ugochukwu also won the Sprint Race at Silverstone and finished the season with two victories and seven podiums on his way to the title.

"This was the main goal at the start of the year, to get the championship," he said after Sunday's race. "I think after quali we knew we did our job, we did the main task, and today, and yesterday, it was just about execution and getting the points and bringing it home."

The title also drew congratulations from seven-time Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton, who visited with the young champ and acknowledged his achievement on Instagram.

Ugochukwu was part of McLaren's driver development program from the age of 13, when the Formula One team signed him to a long-term agreement following his success in karting.

The FIA Formula 3 Championship, which sits immediately below Formula 2, is on the principal development ladder to Formula One, with recent champions Oscar Piastri and Gabriel Bortoleto among those who subsequently progressed to F1.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Union skyrocket as unbeaten streak reaches 11 games
stories.summary: Can anyone stop the Philadelphia Union? Their latest win powered them up the charts in this week's edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday, another weekend of action is in the books, and it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

In one of the most important matches of their end-of-season schedule, Sam Surridge scored in the fourth and 91st minutes to help secure a 2-2 draw against Miami. With the point, Nashville is winless in three (two draws, one defeat) but still in a position to break Inter's Supporters' Shield record with nine games to go.

2. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 2

Nashville further tightened their grip on the Supporters' Shield with a 3-0 win over Chicago on Saturday. A dominant first-half display mixed with some savvy transition attacking in the second half saw all three of the club's designated players find the back of the net.

3. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 3

The Whitecaps took care of business against Salt Lake by a 3-0 scoreline, thoroughly outplaying their hosts. Few teams in the league can match Vancouver for attacking difference-makers, with summer signing Yadaly Diaby making his first league start and notching two goal contributions.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 4

Inching closer to full health, star left back Sergio Reguilón saw the field in the second half as Miami played to a 2-2 draw with San Diego. While the attack still lacks balance without a threat coming down the wings, even a partially hampered Inter Miami squad still boasts some of the sport's best-ever attackers. Lionel Messi and Luis Suárez both found the back of the net Sunday.

5. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Riding the high of his first call-up to the U.S. men's national team, Peyton Miller bagged a brace in the Revolution's 4-2 victory over Orlando on Saturday. With his sizzling speed and developing goal threat, the 18-year-old did well to help lead New England in the absence of the injured Jack Harrison.

6. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 13

Can anyone stop the Union? Despite falling into a three-goal hole on the road in Kansas City, Philadelphia scored four goals in a nine-minute span in the second half to claim a 4-3 win. They've now gone 11 straight games without a loss in league play.

7. LAFC
Previous ranking: 6

Despite taking a 2-0 lead over San Jose in the California Clásico, a 10-man LAFC couldn't hold on for all three points against their in-state rivals. Two second-half concessions, including one late in stoppage time, turned three points into one in a 2-2 draw.

8. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 11

Allan Saint-Maximin opened his Charlotte account with a goal in a 2-1 victory over D.C. United on Saturday. If coach Dean Smith can tap into the former Newcastle man's one-on-one dribbling and his goal threat, Charlotte FC will be a difficult postseason out.

9. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

For more than 45 minutes of action, it looked as if Mateusz Bogusz's penalty conversion had sealed a win for the Dynamo over Cincinnati. However, late in second-half stoppage time, the Polish attacker conceded a penalty that allowed the visitors to equalize at 2-2.

10. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 12

Missing Antoine Griezmann because of a thigh injury suffered in their midweek U.S. Open Cup semifinal defeat, Orlando fell 4-2 to New England. Outside of Lionel Messi, there might not be a player more important to his team's trophy chances than the Frenchman.

11. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 9

A 3-0 loss to Nashville marked seven straight games across all competitions for the Fire without a win. While Robert Lewandowski's scoring record has been positive since he arrived in MLS, it looks as if Chicago's major shift up top has destabilized so much of what propelled them in the spring.

12. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 7

Life has been a slog for New York City lately. A series of poor results over the past two months was extended to include a 1-0 defeat Friday at the hands of their biggest rivals: Red Bull New York. While they created enough chances to win, conversion in front of goal lagged for NYCFC.

13. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 5

Cincinnati left it late but managed to earn a 2-2 road draw against the Dynamo. Kévin Denkey's penalty in the 97th minute rescued the trip, though that doesn't change the fact that Pat Noonan's team has gone five games without a victory.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

After three consecutive victories before this weekend, Dallas played Austin to a 0-0 draw Saturday. Though they created the better chances, Brad Stuver's impressive goalkeeping limited the home side to a solitary point.

15. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 17

It was hardly a dominant showing from the Galaxy, but Greg Vanney's team managed a comeback 3-2 victory on the road in Minnesota, with a makeshift front line that featured Chucky Lozano playing underneath the striker and fullback Harbor Miller back in the attack. Still, all three points count the same.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 16

Thanks to a brace from Anders Dreyer, San Diego earned a 2-2 draw with Miami on Sunday night. While the sophomore outfit still sits below the playoff line out West, they only trail the ninth-placed Portland Timbers by a single point.

17. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 21

Though their summer slide saw San Jose tumble down these rankings, things have stabilized for the Quakes. Their 2-2 draw with LAFC on Saturday marked five straight results, and Timo Werner's return from injury made the outing all the brighter.

18. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 15

Salt Lake were never truly in their match against Vancouver, allowing two goals in the first 30 minutes and failing to ever mount a convincing attack. With Diego Luna now expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury, RSL's path to contention is murkier than at any prior point in the season.

19. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 20

Between his call-up to the U.S. men's national team and his goal to cap off a 1-0 win for Red Bull New York in the Hudson River derby against New York City, Julian Hall has had quite the week. Along the way, Michael Bradley's team defended well for much of Friday's game, which hasn't always been true of them in 2026.

20. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 22

The Sounders' summer signings helped rescue a 3-3 draw in Colorado, with Dejan Joveljić and Caden Clark each nabbing a goal to see their new outfit equalize in Colorado. For a team that's still dealing with a slew of injuries, every point is crucial.

21. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Don't look now, but Austin have managed seven straight results in league play. Most recently, they held Dallas to a scoreless draw thanks to some impressive goalkeeping and possession control. It's not flashy, but there's momentum building for 2027.

22. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 27

The good? New winger Morgan Whittaker scored a brace in his first MLS start and looks the part of a superstar. The bad? The Rapids blew a multigoal lead to draw 3-3 at home with Seattle.

23. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 26

Laurent Courtois' return to Montréal went as well as the interim manager could've hoped. His Columbus team dispatched their hosts -- who double as the Frenchman's former employer -- by a 2-0 scoreline.

24. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 18

Minnesota have dropped points from winning or even positions in each of their past five games, including Saturday's 3-2 home loss to the Galaxy. It's safe to say things have gone off the rails for the Loons.

25. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 19

Every now and then, you come up against a team that puts you in your place. That's what happened for Toronto in their 3-1 loss to St. Louis. There's still a distance for Toronto to go before they're on the level of MLS's best.

26. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 24

The Timbers put up a valiant late-game effort and scored in the 93rd minute, but it wasn't enough to salvage a point in Texas as they stumbled to a 2-1 defeat to Dallas.

27. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 23

While they largely outplayed Charlotte, D.C. still fell 2-1. Even when the team plays well, results still aren't trickling into the nation's capital. D.C. United have just six wins this season, one more than bottom-feeders Montréal and Kansas City.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

There haven't been as many moments of Aleksei Miranchuk magic as Atlanta would've hoped for when they signed him from Atalanta, but the playmaker delivered Saturday. His goal made the difference in the Five Stripes' 1-0 road win over the Timbers.

29. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 29

What looked destined to be a second straight impressive victory for Kansas City turned into a disaster when the hosts conceded four goals in less than 10 minutes to Philadelphia to lose 4-3 on Saturday. Still, André Luiz dominating in the attack after joining this summer is a silver lining.

30. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 30

Up against their old head coach, Courtois, Montréal fell 2-0 at home to the Crew. At least they're through to the Canadian Championship final?

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

They appear to have taken note and their defensive work in New Zealand was outstanding. They will need to be at their very best once more against the Roosters, who have the attacking flair to cause them plenty of problems.

The Roosters were simply too good for the Sharks last week, after going very close to beating the Panthers the week before. They have plenty of experience across the park, with Daly Cherry-Evans putting in a much better performance against the Sharks in combination with the hard running Hugo Savala. Outside those two, the Roosters backline bristles with attacking weapons, with Robert Toia and Mark Nawaqanitawase in unstoppable form, James Tedesco always lurking, and Sam Walker returning at halfback.

But, as we all know, the backs don't win the big games, they just determine the score, and the Roosters have a pack that is the match of any in the league. Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins and Siua Wong were at their destructive best against the Sharks. Add the menace of Victor Radley and Spencer Leniu, plus the returning Angus Crichton, and there isn't a weakness across the middle or on the edges.

The Dolphins will have to match the Roosters forwards, with Thomas Flegler, Tom Gilbert, Max Plath, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, Ray Stone and Francis Molo all in for a big night. If they can negate the Roosters pack, we all know how devastating the Dolphins halves and backs can be.

Cleary has been the focus ever since, as first he avoided suspension for a dangerous contact charge, and then set about rehabilitating an injured foot. The Knights are playing with the casino's money at this stage. After finishing last in 2025, making the finals surpassed anyone's expectations. Phoenix Crossland, Fletcher Sharpe, Kalyn Ponga, Bradman Best, Dan Gagai, Dom Young, the Knights have weapons across the field. Without Jacob Saifiti, they are a little light on up front, but veteran Tyson Frizell has stepped up in the middle and the Knights back-row ranks, strengthened now by the surprise return of Dylan Lucas, have been simply brilliant.

The big question is; can the Knights execute their attacking style against the best defence in the business? They played just the once this season, with the Panthers winning 44-12. We know how good the Panthers are. We have seen them dominate the big games for years. Cleary and Dylan Edwards orchestrating the attack, Isaah Yeo and Liam Martin leading the defence.
